haiku-low.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time F gets a run (pending, or skipped if an active run exists). Older missed fire times are dropped with no history entry.
haiku-low.q2: A run for the new fire time is created with status skipped, already finished with finished_at set, and appears in history. The previous run is unaffected.
haiku-low.q3: It is tried up to 3 times. The wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. After attempt 3 the run is set to failed with finished_at.
haiku-low.q4: After its heartbeat is over 2 minutes stale, the reaper marks the attempt lost. Another worker can claim it after the 1 or 5 minute backoff. The lost attempt counts as used.
haiku-low.q5: The executing job is left alone and finishes normally, or is cancelled instead of retried if it later fails or is lost. The waiting pending run is cancelled. After resume, next_fire_at is recomputed from now, so missed fire times are not caught up.
haiku-low.q6: The UNIQUE (schedule_id, scheduled_for) constraint with INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Also, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED means only one worker gets each schedule.
haiku-low.q7: It is kept in the job_schedule.next_fire_at column. It changes when run creation processes it, and when a schedule is re-enabled or a tenant is resumed.
haiku-low.q8: One atomic statement picks a due pending run with SKIP LOCKED and sets it to running, increments attempt_count, sets heartbeat_at, and inserts a run_attempt row.
haiku-low.q9: It is kept in job_run.heartbeat_at, updated every 30 seconds. The reaper selects running runs whose heartbeat_at is older than 2 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: The wait is recorded in job_run.next_attempt_at, set to now plus 1 or 5 minutes. A claim picks the pending run once next_attempt_at is at or before now().
haiku-low.q11: A job_run row is recorded once per fire time (scheduled_for). A run_attempt row is recorded once per execution try.
haiku-low.q12: Every write requires WHERE status='running' AND attempt_count equals its fencing token. A stale write changes zero rows, so the worker discards its result.

sonnet.q1: Only the most recent of the three fire times gets a run (pending, or skipped if an active run exists). The older two are dropped with no history entry. Run creation then sets next_fire_at to the first fire time after now.
sonnet.q2: A run is still created for it, but with status skipped. It is created already finished (finished_at set) and appears in history. This applies if the previous run is pending (including waiting for a retry) or running.
sonnet.q3: 3 attempts maximum. Wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2 (run goes back to pending with next_attempt_at set). After attempt 3 fails, the run is set to failed with finished_at set. If the schedule is disabled or tenant paused, it is cancelled instead.
sonnet.q4: The reaper picks it up when heartbeat_at is older than 2 minutes. It marks the attempt lost, which counts as a used attempt. Then, if fewer than 3 attempts were used, the run goes pending with the 1 or 5 minute backoff measured from detection, and can then be claimed. At 3 attempts it becomes failed. It is cancelled if schedule disabled or tenant paused.
sonnet.q5: The executing (running) job is left alone and finishes normally; if it later fails or is lost, it becomes cancelled instead of pending. The waiting (pending) job is set to cancelled with finished_at set. Run creation and claiming skip paused tenants, so no runs are created during the pause. On resume, next_fire_at is recomputed to the first fire time after now for each enabled schedule, so nothing missed during the pause is caught up.
sonnet.q6: Run creation selects schedules with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so only one worker gets each schedule. As a backstop, UNIQUE (schedule_id, scheduled_for) with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING yields one run per fire time.
sonnet.q7: In job_schedule.next_fire_at (the next fire time not yet turned into a run). It is set to the first fire time after now when run creation processes the schedule. It is also recomputed on re-enable or tenant resume.
sonnet.q8: One atomic statement selects a pending run with next_attempt_at <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, then sets status = running, increments attempt_count and sets heartbeat_at. It inserts a run_attempt row in the same transaction. Locked rows are skipped by other workers.
sonnet.q9: In job_run.heartbeat_at, updated every 30 seconds by the executing worker while the run is running. The reaper, which runs on every worker, notices running runs with heartbeat_at older than 2 minutes (by database clock).
sonnet.q10: In job_run.next_attempt_at (now() + 1 minute after attempt 1, or + 5 minutes after attempt 2), with status pending. The retry starts when a worker's claim step picks that run once next_attempt_at <= now().
sonnet.q11: One job_run row per fire time (unique on schedule_id plus scheduled_for). One run_attempt row per execution try (up to 3 per run, unique on run_id plus attempt_no).
sonnet.q12: Fencing token. The stale worker's write includes WHERE id = :run AND status = 'running' AND attempt_count = :my_token. After takeover attempt_count has been incremented, so the update changes zero rows, and the worker discards its result. The attempt row is updated only if the run update changed a row.
